nina: quick heads-up — discovered odd auth fallthrough in Go sampleapp when using both REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY. rotation of project key didn't take effect for background workers.

juan: which runtime and sampleapp tag? short repro?

nina: go-sample v1.2.1. repro: set both envs, start worker, rotate project key; worker still calls with org key after reconnect. looks like credential cache picks first-seen key at startup. snippet:
```
REDWOOD_API_KEY=org_live_XX
REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY=proj_live_OLD
# rotate
REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY=proj_live_NEW
# worker reconnects but uses org_live_XX
```

ria: hmm. we've been inconsistent across languages: some SDKs check project-first, some org-first. background jobs + caching makes this worse.

juan: short-term: can we make sampleapps log which key is used and invalidate in-memory creds on SIGHUP so rotation is picked up?

nina: yes I can add SIGHUP handler to flush cache and a startup warning when both envs exist. will open PR to sampleapps.

ops-bot: Created ticket devex/sdk-credentials#4320: "Credential precedence + worker cache invalidation: add SIGHUP flush and startup warning in sampleapps; align SDK precedence"

ria: long-term we should standardize precedence to project-first, but add REDWOOD_PREFER_PROJECT opt-in flag for a safe roll-out. also add telemetry credential.shadow_detected.

juan: agree. I'll draft the opt-in env var for Go and Rust this week. nina — please add the SIGHUP flush so ops can rotate keys without restarting.

nina: will do. PR link when ready.
